title: Irrigation Design, Flow, Pressure, Uniformity & Maintenance
level: Environmental, Irrigation & Fertigation Systems Specialist / advanced specialization development
intendedAudience: Cultivation personnel responsible for irrigation delivery verification, distribution uniformity, filtration/maintenance evidence and safe escalation
prerequisites: Water Quality, Alkalinity, pH, EC & Solution Preparation or equivalent irrigation/fertigation foundation
evidencePolicy: Course uses governed irrigation, root-zone and data-integrity evidence. Nominal emitter ratings, manufacturer schedules and research irrigation treatments are not treated as proof of installed delivery or universal cannabis irrigation prescriptions; actual flow, pressure, uniformity and root-zone response must be verified.
assessmentPolicy: Development-only until technical/assessment review, accessibility review and pilot evidence are complete. Course completion does not authorize protected pressure-system, pump, electrical, plumbing or powered-equipment servicing outside assigned procedures.
description: Develops specialist irrigation-system verification across flow, pressure, distribution uniformity, filtration, clogging, emitter performance, maintenance evidence and command-versus-delivery troubleshooting.
learningOutcomes: Explain how source pressure, regulator performance, line losses, emitter characteristics and filtration affect delivered irrigation and why design specifications do not prove installed performance.
Measure representative emitter output and distribution uniformity using a repeatable sampling plan, appropriate units and controlled comparison conditions.
Diagnose localized and zone-level irrigation faults using flow, pressure, filtration, clogging, controller-command, spatial-pattern and root-zone evidence.
Evaluate preventive maintenance and sanitation needs for filters, emitters and irrigation components while preserving protected-service and chemical-safety boundaries.

Produce a reconstructable irrigation verification and maintenance handoff linking zone identity, command history, measured delivery, pressure/flow evidence, root-zone consequence and authorized next action.
